sentences.text: It serves as the type genus for the order Ichthyosauria and remains one of the best-known ichthyosaur genera today.
Scientists classify Ichthyosaurus as a reptile.
A giant Ichthyosaurus appears in Jules Verne's novel Journey to the Center of the Earth, where it fights and defeats a Plesiosaurus.
The name Ichthyosaurus was first coined by Koenig in 1818.
However, the name was not formally described until later.
Henry Beche and William Conybeare formally described the species Ichthyosaurus communis in 1821, establishing taxonomic priority over earlier names like Proteosaurus.
Fossil evidence of babies inside adults indicates that Ichthyosaurus was viviparous, giving birth to live young.
Three pregnant female specimens of Ichthyosaurus are known, all belonging to the subspecies I. somersetensis.
Although birth orientation is unclear, it is likely that Ichthyosaurus fetuses exited tail-first, a common trait in highly aquatic vertebrates.
The solid bones of Ichthyosaurus ears likely transferred water vibrations to the inner ear.
Ichthyosaurus possessed a fleshy dorsal fin on its back and a large caudal fin.
Researchers suggest Ichthyosaurus was a ram feeder incapable of suction feeding, relying on its jaws and teeth alone to capture prey.
Coprolites of Ichthyosaurus reveal that its diet consisted of fish and squids.
Ichthyosaurus belongs to the family Ichthyosauridae.
Known species of Ichthyosaurus include I. communis (1822), I. breviceps (1881), I. conybeari (1888), I. anningae (2015), I. larkini (2017), and I. somersetensis (2017).
Ichthyosaurus lived from 227.3 to 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Norian to Albian stages.
It is debated how many valid species of Ichthyosaurus exist, as over 50 were attributed to the genus by 1900 before many were moved to separate genera or synonymized.
